owner_login.description: Meant for the owner's login, but GitHub returns the owner as an object the connector does not unpack, so the column stays empty; `full_name` starts with the owner's login.

owner_id.description: Meant for the owner's ID, but GitHub returns the owner as an object the connector does not unpack, so the column stays empty.

owner_type.description: Meant for the owner's type (User or Organization), but GitHub returns the owner as an object the connector does not unpack, so the column stays empty.

stargazers_count.description: Number of users who starred the repository.

watchers_count.description: Number of users who starred the repository, the same as `stargazers_count`: GitHub kept the old name; people watching the repository are in `subscribers_count`.

forks_count.description: Number of forks of the repository.

open_issues_count.description: Open issues of the repository, open pull requests included: GitHub's REST API counts every pull request as an issue.

license_key.description: Meant for the license key, but GitHub returns the license as an object the connector does not unpack, so the column stays empty.

license_name.description: Meant for the license name, but GitHub returns the license as an object the connector does not unpack, so the column stays empty.

topics.description: Meant as comma-separated topics, but GitHub returns an array the connector passes through unchanged, so the column holds JSON array text such as `["a","b"]`.

forks.description: Same value as `forks_count`; GitHub returns both.

open_issues.description: Same value as `open_issues_count`, so it includes open pull requests.

watchers.description: Same value as `watchers_count`: the number of stars, not of watchers.

network_count.description: A count GitHub returns next to `forks_count` without defining it in its REST reference; for the number of forks use `forks_count`.

subscribers_count.description: Number of users watching the repository, that is, getting its notifications; GitHub's `watchers` fields count stars instead.

date.description: The day the connector ran and read the counts; a day it did not run has no row.

stars.description: Stars the repository had on the run day, GitHub's `stargazers_count`.

contributors.description: Contributors on the first page GitHub returned on the run day, so never more than 100.
